title: Q3 FY26 Commitment Matrix & Contingency Playbook for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Renee Ortiz
description:
Purpose: Define a compact, operationally-actionable quarterly commitment matrix for the Hosted API + Model Catalog that maps commitments to SLOs, capacity hedges, experiment lanes, and explicit rollback criteria. This ticket is the canonical PM artifact for Q3 planning: it sets which models/endpoints we commit to, what can be promoted or hedged, staffing and on-call expectations for release windows, and measurable OKR mappings.

Summary of approach:
- Create four commitment lanes: Anchor (must-serve, SLA-backed), Commit (targeted launches with tracked KPIs), Hedge (deferred/backstop models to reduce cost or risk), Experiment (short-lived A/B or eval-driven rollouts).
- For each hosted endpoint and model variant, produce a one-line row describing lane, capacity reservation, canary window, regression-gate thresholds, and primary rollback condition.
- Tie each row to an OKR/initiative and to a technical owner (ENG), SRE lead, and evaluation owner (Applied ML).

Commitment criteria (per model/endpoint):
- Latency SLO: 99th <= configured target (ms) during canary and steady-state.
- Quality gate: benchmarked eval pass-rate >= 92% on production prompt set or no statistically significant regression over baseline.
- Cost guardrail: expected token cost delta vs baseline <= +18% for Commit lanes; Hedge if > +18% unless justified by revenue-generating features.
- Capacity requirement: forecasted 95th percentile QPS falls within Dedicated capacity allotment or Hosted soft-quota; otherwise route to Hedge.

Rollout and fallback policy:
- Canary window: minimum 48 hours at 1-2% traffic, with at least 10K real-user requests (or synthetic equivalent).
- Automatic fallback: Traffic routing layer will revert to the previously committed compatible model if latency or error-rate breach persists for 30 consecutive minutes.
- Manual abort: If quality gate fails during canary, PM/SRE/Applied-ML must meet and decide within 2 hours to rollback or tighten canary.

Contingency hedges and capacity plans:
- Maintain a pool of low-cost quantized variants (Hedge lane) ready to absorb traffic for latency incidents.
- Reserved Dedicated burst slots for top-10 endpoints with pre-approved cost budget to prevent degradation during surge.
- Cross-region fallback: route to secondary region for read-only or low-sensitivity workloads to maintain availability.

OKR mapping (Q3 FY26):
- OKR-1 (Reliability): Ensure 99.9% uptime for Anchor endpoints. All Anchor models must have runbooks and SLA playbooks published.
- OKR-2 (Cost efficiency): Reduce per-token cost of Commit lane endpoints by 12% via quantization or batching suggestions.
- OKR-3 (Developer velocity): Reduce time-to-canary to < 48 hours for non-Anchor models via automation and preflight checks.

Staffing and run cadence:
- Releases will be executed during a weekly release window (Thursdays 16:00-20:00 PT) with a nominated on-call SRE and EM present.
- Staffing: 2x Eng owners, 1x SRE, 1x Applied ML, 1x QA per Commit lane. Anchor lanes require 1 extra SRE backup.

Acceptance criteria for PM commitment matrix:
- A CSV/Google Sheet (row-per-endpoint) exists with columns: endpoint, model-variant, lane, latency-target, quality-gate, cost-delta-estimate, capacity-reserve, canary-window, owners, OKR link, PR link.
- All Anchor endpoints have verified runbook links and a slated on-call rotation.
- Stakeholder signoff (Eng, SRE, Applied ML, Security) captured on the sheet.

Cross-functional dependencies:
- Kernel tuning and quantization work (ENG-19873) for cost hedges.
- Console rollout for per-route cost breakdown (ENG-24321).
- Eval harness updates to include production prompt sets (PM-45102).

Next steps:
1) Populate the commitment matrix template with top-40 endpoints by QPS by 2026-03-19.
2) Run a 1-week sensitivity analysis to identify >18% cost-delta risks by 2026-03-26.
3) Schedule a stakeholder gating meeting (PM/ENG/SRE/Applied ML) on 2026-03-29 to lock anchors and commitments.
